notes: The supplied ball-and-interval cover argument proves both clauses of N002 from the conditional premise N001. Positive enlarged radii handle zero-diameter members, and the nonnegative-sum argument preserves the required strict final bound. No external E applications occur.

applicability.notes: S001 applies N001 with p=q>0, scale r/2>0 and tolerance ε/2>0 under L1,L2. S004 uses its explicitly exported countable reindexing provision. S006 applies its zero-measure criterion to the max metric product with its Borel structure, exponent q+1>0, and arbitrary Δ,τ>0. The routine background below has all its conditions available.

argument.notes: S002 enlarges each finite diameter within r with summable error, and S003 gives Σa_i^q<ε. In S004, pairwise metric bounds prove finite extended diameters ≤2a_i, so these are admissible covers rather than artifacts of toReal(∞)=0. The interval count satisfies N_i≤2/a_i, yielding the stated 2^(q+2) cost constant in S005. S006 produces admissible covers at every positive scale with arbitrarily small cost. Empty members, zero diameters, empty A or X, and singleton spaces cause no exception.

statement_closure.notes: The input specifies finite-scale admissibility, empty-member costs, zero-measure equivalence and reindexing. D001–D005,D007,D012 and the local declarations determine all objects actually used. N002 exports both the universally quantified quantitative cover and the zero-measure conclusion for arbitrary metric X,A and q>0, with the max metric and constant depending only on q. Canonical Borel structures add no measurability condition on A.

background_notes.fact: For real q>0, x↦x^q on [0,∞), with 0^q=0, is continuous and increasing. Given 0≤d<r and η>0, some a satisfies d<a<r and a^q<d^q+η. For positive a, (2/a)(2a)^(q+1)=2^(q+2)a^q.

grounds.reason: L1 gives q>0; L2 gives r>0 and ε>0.
The finite cover gives 0≤d_i≤r/2<r, and η=ε·2^(−i−2)>0.
The chosen radii satisfy a_i>0, the domain needed for the positive-base power laws.

background_notes.justification: On positive arguments define x^q=exp(q log x); continuity, monotonicity, and product and exponent laws follow from the corresponding real exponential and logarithm properties. At zero, x^q→0 for q>0. Right continuity at d permits a positive increment smaller than r−d with power change less than η. The displayed identity follows by expanding positive-base powers and cancelling a.

background_notes.fact: For nonnegative countable families, sums are suprema of finite subsums. Termwise inequalities pass to sums, and sums distribute over addition and multiplication by finite nonnegative constants. Also Σ_{i≥0}2^(−i−2)=1/2.

grounds.reason: All a_i^q,d_i^q and error terms are nonnegative and satisfy the pointwise error bound.

background_notes.justification: Finite subsum inequalities persist under suprema. For addition, finite index sets can be enlarged to a common finite set; multiplication by a finite nonnegative constant preserves these suprema. The first m error weights sum to (1−2^(−m))/2, whose increasing limit is 1/2. Thus Σa_i^q≤Σd_i^q+ε/2<ε; no strict infinite termwise comparison is asserted.

background_notes.fact: If a set has finite extended diameter d, each pairwise distance is ≤d. A closed ball of nonnegative radius a has all pairwise distances ≤2a, hence extended diameter ≤2a. If sets in two metric factors have pairwise bounds b,c, their product in the max metric has extended diameter ≤max(b,c).

grounds.reason: D002 defines extended diameter as a supremum.
D003 identifies finite extended diameters with their real values.
D007 supplies the max distance formula.
D012 supplies the ball membership inequalities.
Every U_i has finite diameter d_i.
Centers lie in nonempty U_i, radii are positive, and interval length is ≤a_i.

background_notes.justification: Each distance is bounded by its defining supremum. For points in a ball, the triangle inequality through the center bounds distance by a+a. Taking suprema retains this finite bound, including for empty sets. The max metric formula gives the product bound pointwise, then by the same supremum argument. This also proves U_i⊆K_i and finite extended diameter of every constructed block.

background_notes.fact: For 0<a≤1, N=ceil(1/a) is a positive natural number with 1/N≤a and N≤1/a+1≤2/a. The N closed intervals [j/N,(j+1)/N], 0≤j<N, cover [0,1] and each has diameter 1/N.

grounds.reason: N_i and the intervals have these definitions.

background_notes.justification: The ceiling inequalities give 1/a≤N≤1/a+1; positive division yields the claimed bounds. For t∈[0,1), choose j=floor(Nt), obtaining 0≤j<N and j/N≤t<(j+1)/N; t=1 belongs to the last interval. Endpoint differences give interval diameter 1/N.

background_notes.fact: In ordinary classical mathematics, a countably indexed collection of nonempty sets admits a selection. This applies to the admissible radii for each i and, separately, to U_i only on the indices where U_i is nonempty.

grounds.reason: The right-continuity argument establishes a nonempty set of admissible radii for each natural i.
For each index restricted by U_i≠∅, a center exists by nonemptiness.

background_notes.justification: The standard countable choice principle selects one element from each established nonempty set. The second index set is a subset of ℕ; if it is empty the selection is the empty function. No choice of a point in an empty U_i, or an unconditional point of X, is made.

background_notes.fact: For nonnegative costs c_{i,j} with natural finite row lengths N_i, the sum over {(i,j):j<N_i} equals Σ_i Σ_{j<N_i}c_{i,j}. Termwise upper bounds may be summed even before proving finiteness of either sum.

grounds.reason: F004 supplies finite natural row lengths N_i and finite block diameters.
Block costs at positive exponent q+1 and their upper bounds are nonnegative; F003 supplies the finite strict upper bound Σa_i^q<ε.

background_notes.justification: Every finite collection of pairs lies in finitely many rows, and a finite union of complete finite rows is finite. Taking suprema of finite sums in both directions gives the identity. Taking suprema of finite termwise inequalities gives the inequalities in S005, with no exchange of signed or conditionally convergent series.
